section.title: File & command fence
section.subtitle: Limit where writes may go: writable folders, protected paths, network switch and enforcement backend
field.mode.label: Where this session may write
field.mode.option.danger-full-access: No fence (same as turning this protection off)
field.mode.help: Changes only the session you have open; each session keeps its own level. Day to day, leave it here: normal workspace reads, writes and commands are not blocked, only out-of-bounds writes, edits to protected files, and network use while the switch is off.
field.defaultMode.label: Where new sessions may write
field.defaultMode.help: Affects only sessions created later; sessions already open keep their own level.
field.onUnavailable.label: When the backend cannot start
field.onUnavailable.option.degrade: Degrade to the policy fence (keep working, approvals catch it)
field.onUnavailable.option.fail-closed: Refuse: all writes and exec (reads still work)
field.onUnavailable.help: Applies only to the two real-isolation backends, docker and the Windows restricted token: when they cannot start, either degrade to the in-process policy fence and keep going, or refuse writes and exec. partial on the in-process policy fence is expected and is not affected by this setting.
field.networkAccess.label: Network access
field.networkAccess.help: When off, network commands are refused (curl / wget / npm install / git pull and the like). The switch only stops network actions written in the command itself; requests inside a script are not caught.
field.networkAllowlist.label: Outbound allowlist (domains, semicolon separated)
field.networkAllowlist.help: The proxy of the windows-token backend's second tier (after the elevated setup) lets through only these entries; *.example.com matches subdomains, an exact domain does not. An empty list allows nothing even with the network on.
field.extraWritableRoots.label: Extra writable roots (semicolon separated)
field.extraWritableRoots.help: Allow a few more folders besides the workspace and the private temp directory. Relative paths resolve from the session working directory.
field.readOnlySubpaths.label: Read-only subpaths (semicolon separated)
field.readOnlySubpaths.help: Exceptions inside the writable roots: these subtrees are refused even when they sit under a writable root.
field.backend.label: Enforcement backend
field.backend.option.windows-token: Windows restricted token (Windows only; the system blocks out-of-bounds writes)
field.backend.option.docker: Container (needs docker on this machine, enforcement full)
field.backend.help: The restricted-token backend runs commands in a runner subprocess with a restricted token and workspace ACLs (no docker needed; the system refuses out-of-bounds writes inside commands; known gaps: hardlink aliases, reads are unrestricted, real network control needs the one-time elevated setup). The container backend runs commands inside docker (only the workspace is mounted, the network follows the switch above), which suits cross-platform build commands. Commands whose shell shape cannot be recognised keep their executor and still run on the host.
field.image.label: Container image
field.image.help: The image the container backend uses, {image} by default. It has to contain the tools your command needs (node:20-alpine, for example).
field.enforcement.label: Enforcement level for this session
field.backendStatus.label: Backend status
field.tmpDir.label: Sandbox private temp directory
field.effective.label: In effect now
field.denials.label: Last 3 refusals
field.probe.label: Probe the backend now
field.probe.help: Probes once with the backend chosen above: whether the container is usable and which level it falls back to; the result is the line right under the button.
field.networkTier.label: Network second tier (elevated setup)
field.setup.label: Install network control with elevation (one UAC prompt)
field.setup.help: Creates a dedicated offline account, blocks outbound traffic by that account's SID (5 firewall rules plus 12 persistent WFP filters) and stores the password with DPAPI; the account stays disabled until every step succeeds. You need to click Allow once in the UAC prompt.
field.uninstall.label: Uninstall network control (one UAC prompt)
field.uninstall.help: Removes what the elevated setup installed: the dedicated account and its group, the 5 firewall rules, the 12 persistent WFP filters (provider and sublayer included), then deletes setup-state.json / account.bin / setup-error.txt. You need to click Allow once in the UAC prompt.
field.doctor.label: Check the network second tier
field.doctor.help: Checks item by item: FFI, state file, account, password decryptable, firewall rules, WFP sublayer; all green means full.
field.problems.label: Config problems (defaults used instead)
field.problems.help: A bad sandbox config never disables workspace writes entirely — it only costs one layer of fencing — so the defaults are used here and the problems are listed as they are.
review.group.title: Change preview
review.group.description: See which lines change before a file is written or edited
review.field.enabled.label: Enable preview before edit
review.field.enabled.help: When off, no diff is posted into the conversation; tools still run and approvals are still asked. Turning the whole fence off stops previews too.
review.field.maxLines.label: Lines shown per preview
review.field.maxLines.help: Anything past this many lines is not shown; the end states how many lines are left (default {lines}).
review.field.contextLines.label: Context lines around each change
review.field.contextLines.help: Same idea as -U in `diff -u`: 0 shows only the change itself, 3 is the default. Those context lines are what tell you which function changed.
review.field.chain.label: Where it sits in the chain
review.field.chain.text: order 25: earlier than the approval card (30), so you already see what will change before you click Allow; it never blocks and never clears other guards (it always defers).
review.field.stats.label: This mount's counter
review.field.stats.text: {emitted} previews sent, {truncated} of them cut off by the line limit.

save.badOnUnavailable: “When the backend cannot start” must be degrade (keep going) or fail-closed (refuse writes and exec)
save.badBackend: The backend must be policy (policy fence), docker (container) or windows-token (Windows restricted token)

save.imageSpace: The image name cannot contain spaces
